screening_decisions.reason: Explicitly described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial evaluating the systemic immunomodulator inosiplex in patients with alopecia totalis. Meets the RCT and intervention criteria.
Randomized, placebo-controlled trial of weekly oral prednisolone pulse therapy for extensive alopecia areata. Meets RCT and systemic intervention criteria.

Multicenter, prospective, randomized, controlled, investigator-blinded trial comparing two topical corticosteroid formulations for mild-to-moderate alopecia areata. Meets RCT and topical intervention criteria.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled study of 3% topical minoxidil for extensive alopecia areata, alopecia totalis, and alopecia universalis. Meets RCT and topical intervention criteria.
Patients were assigned to one of two treatment regimens in a double-blind manner (minoxidil vs placebo then crossover), constituting an RCT evaluating topical minoxidil for extensive alopecia areata.
Randomized double-blind design treating half-scalp with DPCP plus either 5% minoxidil or vehicle, evaluating topical interventions for chronic severe alopecia areata. Meets RCT criteria.

Twenty-six patients were randomly assigned to receive topical cyclosporine, PUVA, or intravenous thymopentin, evaluating topical/systemic interventions for alopecia totalis/universalis nonresponders. Meets RCT criteria.

Six patients had different concentrations of ALA and vehicle applied to separate scalp areas without mention of randomization or a control group. This appears to be an uncontrolled, non-randomized within-patient comparison and does not meet the RCT criterion.
Patients were randomized to receive topical cyclosporin A in a liposomal vehicle or vehicle alone, constituting an RCT of a topical intervention for alopecia areata.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled study of systemic imipramine for alopecia areata. Meets RCT and intervention criteria.

Thirty patients were randomly assigned to topical immunotherapy, systemic interferon alpha, or combination therapy in a trial evaluating topical/systemic interventions for chronic severe alopecia areata. Meets RCT criteria.
Double-blind study of topical cyclosporin A versus placebo in 85 patients with alopecia areata, constituting an RCT of a topical intervention.
Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of a new topical clobetasol propionate foam formulation for moderate-to-severe alopecia areata. Meets RCT and topical intervention criteria.
Randomized, controlled trial of a systemic steroid taper followed by topical minoxidil or vehicle in patients with alopecia areata, including alopecia totalis/universalis. Meets RCT criteria.

The abstract appears to summarize prior studies and long-term follow-up observations rather than report a new primary RCT. It mentions a prior double-blind placebo-controlled year-long study, but this abstract itself does not present a distinct randomized trial. Therefore it does not meet the RCT criterion for inclusion at title/abstract screening.

A controlled trial comparing squaric acid dibutylester, diphencyprone, minoxidil, and placebo in patchy alopecia areata. Although the abstract does not explicitly state 'randomized', the term 'controlled trial' with multiple therapeutic arms and placebo suggests it may be an RCT; conservatively included for full-text review.
Cross-sectional questionnaire study assessing illness perceptions and quality of life. No intervention evaluated and not an RCT.
Methodological commentary discussing when RCTs are unnecessary. Not a trial evaluating an intervention for alopecia areata.
Randomized, double-blind, controlled trial evaluating topical essential oil aromatherapy versus carrier oil control for alopecia areata. Meets RCT and topical intervention criteria.
Narrative review/update article summarizing pathogenesis and treatments. Not a primary RCT.
Retrospective population-based epidemiological study assessing incidence and natural history. Not an intervention trial or RCT.
Observational cohort study evaluating prognostic factors in patients treated with diphenylcyclopropenone. No control group and no randomization described; not an RCT.

Patients were divided into three matched groups but randomization is not mentioned. The design appears non-randomized and comparative rather than an RCT, so it does not meet the explicit RCT criterion.
Review article focusing on genetic basis of alopecia areata. Not an intervention trial.
Methodological paper discussing quality assessment of controlled trials in general. Not a trial of an intervention for alopecia areata.
